items.title: 2 Big Food Dividends Were Just Cut. 3 More Quietly Stopped Growing.
items.summary: Conagra and Campbell's already made their moves, but several other legacy food giants are sending quieter signals that income investors have learned to recognize too late. Three warning patterns separate a frozen payout from the next cut.

items.title: Can General Mills' Brazil Exit Sharpen Its Portfolio Strategy?
items.summary: GIS' Brazil sale advances portfolio simplification, sharpening its focus on higher-growth businesses while supporting debt reduction.

items.title: 3 Consumer Stocks Walking a Fine Line
items.summary: Consumer staples stocks are solid insurance policies in frothy markets ripe for corrections. On the other hand, they usually underperform during bull runs, and this paradigm has rung true over the past six months as the sector’s -5.1% decline paled in comparison to the S&P 500’s 11.7% gain.

items.title: Tyson Foods, MGP Ingredients, Conagra, Flowers Foods, and General Mills Shares Are Falling, What You Need To Know
items.summary: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after national cattle shortages and volatile livestock prices squeezed operating margins and prompted outlook cuts across the food production industry.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Sept. 3: Campbell's Stock Slumps on Weaker Profit and Sales Miss
items.summary: On Sept. 3, 2026, the packaged-food maker cut its dividend 36% and outlined a $500 million cost-savings plan to offset margin pressure.

items.title: Campbell’s Slides 9% on 36% Dividend Cut, General Mills Falls 4%, Kraft Heinz Drops 3%
items.summary: Campbell's just slashed its dividend and reset guidance well below Wall Street's bar, and the fallout is spreading fast to peers that haven't reported a single number yet.

items.title: There's no end in sight for Campbell's quarterly sales declines: AlphaSpace
items.summary: Market Catalysts host Julie Hyman uses the AlphaSpace platform to take a closer look at one of Thursday's trending stories: Campbell's (CPB) reporting its fourth consecutive drop in quarterly sales.

items.title: Hormel vs. General Mills: Don’t Let the Bigger Dividend Check Fool You
items.summary: Hormel and General Mills both cut big dividend checks and carry identical payout ratios, yet one of these grocery giants has a streak the other can never match. Knowing which metric to prioritize could change which stock belongs in your portfolio.
